content.comment_body: When I choose [Message texts] and add an ON/OFF block, I can't modify the display next to the 'input name for status FALSE' or 'input name for status TRUE'. I am able to edit the text, but pressing OK does nothing. This issue did not occur with [product_name] [version_no] before.
I couldn't reproduce the error you described. Please refer to the video I attached.

If I recall correctly, this bug was present in [version_no] as well. @ixo65, try removing the 'e' in 'false', and you'll see you can't click OK. The workaround I've found is: after deleting the 'e', mark the field and press space to add a blank character, and then OK works. Watch at 0:26 in the video—OK does nothing. At 0:30, I press space, and then OK responds.

Your video helped a lot. I was able to reproduce your steps on my computer. For me, [product_name] [version_no] does not show this problem. However, [product_name] [version_no] does have this issue when deleting using DEL or BACKSPACE, regardless of hardware or text content. Using SPACE does not cause the issue. I think this is worth submitting a support request. Thanks for your assistance. [user_name]
On both [version_no], I am able to delete with DEL or BACKSPACE without any trouble.
I'm using Windows 10 Pro x64, in case it helps to narrow down the bug. Not sure if it appears on Windows 7, for example. EDIT: Java V8 build 111 (build 1.8.0_111-b14).

That's quite curious. It seems there's something unique in certain installations of this software causing the issue. It's hard to pinpoint the source, especially since my [version_no] doesn't show the problem, but [version_no] does. Personally, I doubt it's related to Java VM. I run Windows 7 Professional with [product_name] directly, using Java V8 Update 91 (build 1.8.0_91-b14).
I'm on Win7 Pro 64bit (build 7601) and Java V8 Update 111 (build 1.8.0_111).

I've updated my Java to V8 Update 111, but the result remains unchanged. It's hard to determine what other software might influence this behavior. For me, the workaround of pressing SPACEBAR to delete is sufficient. Confirmed: Windows 7 Professional 64bit (build 7601).

You're correct, [user_name]. I can't reproduce this bug in [version_no], so it's an issue specific to [version_no]. I can deal with it, but it was confusing when editing text and OK wouldn't respond after multiple attempts.
Thank you all! I'm new to [product_name], and small issues like this are especially frustrating for beginners. I would've never discovered that workaround myself. You all deserve a break today—LOL.

analysis.insight_summary: Users have encountered a bug in [product_name] [version_no] where deleting all text in a message block input using DEL or BACKSPACE prevents the OK button from functioning, making it impossible to confirm changes. This problem doesn't appear in [product_name] [version_no] for most users and seems related to specific installations or operating environments. The bug is inconsistent and difficult to reproduce universally, with the only reliable workaround being to insert a space character instead of deleting all text.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to freely edit or delete message text fields and confirm changes using the OK button, as was the case in previous versions of the software.
